claims.text: 店は動物性食材を一切使用しない100%ヴィーガン業態で、大豆ミートも使わずオリジナルの豆ベースパティを使用しているとされる。
動物性食材不使用・大豆ミート不使用を明記した100%ヴィーガン専門店。

name: サラダボウル専門店 ウィズグリーン 新宿三丁目店 (With Green Shinjuku Sanchome)

claims.text: The shop offers a vegetarian/vegan-compatible dressing option (e.g. a lemon-based dressing), and diners can build a fully vegetable bowl by choosing their own toppings.

name: 焼きあご塩らー麺 たかはし 新宿本店 (Yakiago Shio Ramen Takahashi, Shinjuku Main )

claims.text: The tare (sauce base) is made with Sekigahara tamari soy sauce combined with a large amount of dried sardines (niboshi) as the signature flavor component.

The signature broth is built on pork bone and chicken carcass stock combined with grilled flying fish (yakiago), dried sardines, and kelp — meat- and fish-based throughout, with no vegan broth alternative found.

name: 麺㐂 やしま 円山町店 (Yashima Maruyamacho-ten (Menki Yashima))

claims.text: The udon broth is a Kansai-style dashi made with bonito (katsuobushi), used throughout the menu, including for tempura dipping sauces.
The restaurant lists a specific, priced vegetarian course (4,400 yen) as a standing menu option rather than an off-menu special-request-only accommodation.

No information is available about cross-contamination controls. With only 16 seats and an open counter kitchen, shared preparation surfaces for wheat-containing dishes (pastry, flour-thickened sauces, Bánh Mì bread) are likely.

The menu blends French and ethnic Asian influences (Hainanese chicken rice, Nasi Goreng, Bánh Mì), making standard soy sauce a plausible ingredient, though its specific use has not been confirmed in any source reviewed.
All reviewed sources confirm the menu is built around meat, fish, and classical French dairy. No vegan-safe preparation protocol is mentioned.
No allergy-handling procedures or staff training information appears in any source. Reservations are made by phone the day before, which is the logical opportunity to communicate dietary needs.
Omakase course format (menu decided day-of based on freshest available ingredients) may allow ingredient-level customisation if communicated clearly at reservation time.

name: あなご料理 柊 本店 (Anago Ryori Hiiragi Honten)

claims.text: Tempura is a core menu item; wheat flour is used in the batter. No dedicated fryer or separate wheat-free cooking line is mentioned across any source reviewed.
Standard wheat-containing soy sauce is the default condiment and marinade base for grilled and simmered anago preparations. No tamari or gluten-free shoyu alternative is mentioned.
The entire menu is built around fish and seafood; all broths and sauces derive from anago and dashi. There is no plant-based cooking line.
No allergy handling procedures or allergen menu are documented on any available source. Direct contact by phone (079-284-1239) before visiting is strongly advised for any dietary restriction.

White-grilled anago (白焼き) is a minimal-ingredient preparation that showcases the eel without heavy saucing — if diners can confirm no shoyu marinade is applied and the piece is cooked on a clean surface, this could be the lowest-wheat item on the menu.
No dedicated gluten-free preparation area or protocols mentioned in any source; standard Italian kitchen with pasta, pizza, and bread service means wheat cross-contamination is a realistic concern.
No soy sauce identified in sourced menu descriptions; cuisine is Italian, but wheat is present throughout via pasta, pizza dough, and bread. No gluten-free alternatives noted anywhere.
Dairy (butter, cream, cheese) and meat products are core to the menu. Basil butter is served as a standard bread accompaniment. No vegan-safe preparation protocols mentioned.
No allergy handling protocols or allergen menu documented in any fetched source. Direct phone contact (079-222-5511) is the only confirmed path to obtain allergy accommodation information.
Small independent restaurant with a close-knit team (reportedly one owner, one chef), which may allow flexible accommodation requests if arranged in advance by phone.
